content: 1. Drug Interactions with Omeprazole: Pentobarbital: Reduces the effectiveness of omeprazole by altering CYP2C19 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Pexidartinib: Omeprazole decreases pexidartinib absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If necessary, administer pexidartinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after H2-receptor antagonists or antacids. Phenobarbital: Reduces omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Phenytoin: Decreases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phytoestrogens: Omeprazole reduces phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Polysaccharide Iron: Omeprazole decreases iron absorption by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. Ponatinib: Omeprazole reduces ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. Posaconazole: Omeprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH, while posaconazole increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Primidone: Reduces omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Quazepam: Omeprazole increases quazepam levels by reducing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Ribociclib: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Rifampin: Reduces omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Rifapentine: Similar to rifampin, it decreases omeprazole levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Rilpivirine: Omeprazole reduces rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially leading to treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. Riociguat: Omeprazole decreases riociguat levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Rose Hips: Omeprazole reduces rose hips levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. Ruxolitinib: Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Sotorasib: Omeprazole reduces sotorasib absorption. Avoid co-administration or administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after antacids. St. John’s Wort: Reduces omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely. Stiripentol: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Tacrolimus: Omeprazole increases tacrolimus levels, especially in poor CYP2C19 metabolizers. Monitor closely. Tazemetostat: Omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Theophylline: Prolonged use of omeprazole may increase theophylline toxicity due to changes in gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for toxicity. Thyroid Desiccated: Omeprazole reduces thyroid hormone absorption by increasing gastric pH. Conflicting evidence exists; monitor closely. Tinidazole: Omeprazole increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tofacitinib: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust dose if co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. Triazolam: Omeprazole increases triazolam levels by reducing metabolism. Monitor closely. Triclabendazole: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tucatinib: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or adjust doses as per product labeling. Vismodegib: Omeprazole reduces vismodegib bioavailability by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. Voriconazole: Increases omeprazole levels via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Warfarin: Omeprazole may increase warfarin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor INR frequently and adjust warfarin dose as needed. 2. Adverse Effects: Acute Tubulointerstitial Nephritis (TIN): Can occur at any point during therapy. Symptoms may include malaise, nausea, and decreased renal function. Discontinue therapy if TIN is suspected. Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions (SCAR): Includes Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Discontinue therapy at the first sign of SCAR. Clostridioides difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD): May occur up to two months after therapy initiation. Discontinue therapy if CDAD is confirmed and provide appropriate treatment. Cutaneous and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Therapy may trigger new-onset or exacerbate existing autoimmune conditions. Discontinue therapy if symptoms develop. Chromogranin A (CgA) Levels: Omeprazole-induced changes in gastric acidity may increase CgA levels, leading to false-positive results in neuroendocrine tumor diagnostics. Reassess CgA levels 14 days after discontinuation. 3. Special Considerations: Pregnancy: Omeprazole may cause fetal harm based on animal studies. It is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless necessary. Breastfeeding: Weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the potential risks of therapy to the infant. Administration: Take omeprazole with food and a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew capsules. Avoid alcohol during therapy. 4. General Advice: Avoid prescribing omeprazole in the absence of a proven bacterial infection to reduce the risk of drug resistance. Monitor patients closely for adverse effects and drug interactions, especially when co-administering with other medications.
